sentences.text: Ms. Medha Pande, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Sachin, learned counsel for the applicant.
Mr. Deepak Bisht, AGA with Ms. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.

Applicant Jugraj Singh Alias Gopi, who is in judicial custody in Case Crime No.0026 of 2022, under Sections 365, 363, 366, 376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Khatima, District Udham Singh Nagar, has sought his release on bail.

entities.text: Police Station Khatima, District Udham Singh Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant/accused would submit that the FIR was registered against the applicant/accused by the mother of the prosecutrix; that, the prosecutrix was examined as PW1 in the Trial Court wherein she has unequivocally stated that she does not know the applicant/accused;
that, the applicant/accused never made any call to her and she was not chatting with him and he did not commit any sexual assault upon her body.

4. Learned counsel would further submit that in the cross-examination also the prosecutrix stuck to her guns and stated that she gave the statement against the applicant/accused at the instance and asking of the Police.

She would further that the mother of the prosecutrix was examined as PW2 and in her statement she deposed before the Court that her daughter i.e. the prosecutrix had gone to her maternal grandmother and no offence of sexual assault was made upon her by the applicant/accused.
She would further submit that similar statement was given by father of the prosecutrix who was examined as PW3.
5. Learned State Counsel would fairly admit to it.

6. In view of the above, but, without expressing any opinion about merits of the case before the Trial Court, this Court is of the view that this is a fit case for bail.
7.
The bail application is, accordingly, allowed.
Let the applicant be released on furnishing bail bond with two sureties in the amount of  35,000/- and personal bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned.
